suggestions.title: What a bad trip is and isn't: a "this is not X, it's Y" correction with lists
suggestions.reading: As the guide has it, each read after the Human first half of Psychological First Aid and the section's heading: [47%](https://www.pangram.com/history/d220fe49-34b5-4fd2-bfb0-7fb7ae415b88).
suggestions.tested:
1. "A bad trip doesn't mean you're broken or being punished, or that you're unspiritual or impure or damaged for good, it just means too much came at once for your nervous system and your body and the way you make sense of things, whether from the setting, old memories, the dose or the people around you. The response is care rather than blame." [56%](https://www.pangram.com/history/7a430213-f2a0-4783-b81d-7ca1af0ef7ef). This is the move that read Human on The Other Bypass, the pair joined with "it just means".

2. "A bad trip does not prove that you are broken, punished, unspiritual, impure, or permanently damaged. It just means more came at you than your nervous system, your body and the part of you that makes sense of things could handle, whether it came from the setting, your memories, the dose, or the people in your life. The response is care rather than blame." [100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/26e09bff-ea01-42e4-9a26-63741d105f39).

3. "Having a bad trip doesn't make you broken, and it doesn't mean you're being punished, or that you're unspiritual or impure, or damaged for good. It just means too much hit you at once. Your nervous system and your body got flooded and your mind couldn't make sense of it all, and the setting, old memories, the dose or what's going on with the people around you could all have fed into that. So be kind about it, to yourself or to whoever's going through it, because blaming anyone only makes it heavier." [100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/d37ffa07-6a40-44f1-ac90-5bc92ac5be14). Every sentence here was fixed the way three AI readers agreed.
suggestions.why: It reads AI in every wording I've tried, and it has the shape most of the stuck paragraphs share: "this is not X, it's Y", with lists of five to seven words and a short verdict at the end. You named the pattern on round 1 ("X does not Y" is "super ai"). The same shape is in Spiritual ≠'s bypassing and practice pair, the Fear/Panic Loop, the demons' hooks and "unhookable", the helper's "not there to" list, the touch part's "Compassion does not mean ...", When the Trip Feels Amazing's "Bliss is not proof of safety", and After the Storm's fruit of insight.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: write it the way you'd say it. What it says has to stay: a bad trip isn't proof you're broken, punished, unspiritual, impure or damaged for good. It means too much came at once, for the nervous system, the body or the sense of things, from the setting, memories, the dose or the people around you, and it calls for care, not blame. I'll carry what you do to the seven paragraphs above, test each, and put the ones that read Human straight in.

suggestions.title: The day after: a run of short commands and don'ts
suggestions.reading: As the guide has it, each read after the Human first half of Psychological First Aid and the section's heading: [94%](https://www.pangram.com/history/16f40cc5-6d75-42ab-be39-06594e2a96af).
suggestions.tested:
1. "Don't rush to turn a hard experience into content, your system just needs time to settle. Sleep, eat something simple, drink some water and take a walk. Journaling helps, and so does praying and meditating gently. Talk it over with one grounded person rather than twenty chaotic ones. And for now, hold off on huge decisions, and don't diagnose yourself from one intense night or assume every vision was literal and every fear was false." [100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/3f119bf6-0f14-4273-b5d7-2240205518ea). This try puts the reason first and breaks up the run.

2. "Don't rush to turn a hard experience into content. Sleep, eat simple food, drink water, go for a walk, journal, and pray or meditate gently. Talk with one grounded person, rather than twenty chaotic people. Don't make huge decisions, diagnose yourself from one intense night, or assume every vision was literal and every fear was false. Let the system settle." [100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/66c34e9c-5b54-47d5-9c2d-cceb608b7425). Here the one-word steps are joined into one sentence.
